questions.q: Why is your ego never satisfied, according to lesson 1?
a: It keeps comparing you with people who have more
It only cares about the distant past
It fears every kind of success
It stops working when you are calm
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the ego measures worth by wealth, looks and status against others.

questions.q: What triggered Dan Harris to start looking into his own mind?
a: A panic attack on live television
A bad review of his first book
Losing his job at the network
A retreat gifted by a friend
questions.why: The overview describes his on-air panic attack as the turning point.

questions.q: What does lesson 2 say about letting go of your ego?
a: It does not make you a pushover
It means giving up on ambition
It requires you to stop negotiating
It makes you lose creativity
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues mindfulness makes you more creative and productive, not weak.

questions.q: Which three habitual responses does lesson 3 say we normally have?
a: Wanting something, rejecting it, or zoning out
Fighting, fleeing, or freezing
Planning, doubting, or delaying
Praising, blaming, or ignoring
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists want it, reject it and zone out.

questions.q: What is the fourth response that meditation offers?
a: Observing without judging
Acting immediately
Doubling down on desire
Suppressing the feeling
questions.why: Lesson 3 says meditation gives you a pause to observe without judging.
